findings: Original SimInfo.fromDic converts isSelf string false into boolean true via bool(nonempty string); a non-self hit can become self when wrong-type serialized input reaches model boundary. Reproduced boundary only, not server input reachability.

Original integer conversion failure is swallowed and retains bad-int as Asset.autoId. Malformed JSON EXIF remains not-json string rather than raising. Downstream code expects model attributes; successful construction does not prove valid schema.

Original fromDB skips basic scalar conversion in fast path: string 123 remains string for integer autoId. Real SQLite INTEGER rows usually give int; this control injects wrong-type row to establish boundary behavior.

25 original model methods pass with explicit module namespace and adapters; include nested models/list numeric conversions/JSON/enum/error cases. They do not cover false-string bool, invalid scalar retention or malformed nested JSON boundaries.
Three DB methods in original tests catch all Exception and turn failure into skip; assertions also raise Exception. Such skips cannot prove DB schema/EXIF/relation correctness. No DB method run here.

test_fetchExInfo uses fixed asset ID and catches all failures, printing failure without rethrow; missing batch asset merely prints. Script exit success does not imply successful metadata retrieval. Source finding, script unexecuted.

TestAutoDbField class whole source read, including nested defaults/string conversion/proxy persistence checks; this class not executed this batch. Prior failing-persistence/default-sharing controls remain separate.

model_speed.py setup_simple_test_db creates12 columns but Insert Values has13 placeholders for12 supplied values; run_all_tests first calls nonexistent log.setLog from reviewed util/log.py. Source defects, benchmark unexecuted.

Benchmark always runs dict path before model path, compares dictionaries vs richer typed models without output-parity assertions, uses time.time and means; no controlled alternating performance evidence. No speedup accepted.
Json converts literal string null values to None; enum unknown strings and unrecognized field shapes remain permissive. Scalar/list semantics require explicit downstream qualification.
